# v3.01-dev

Deleting a user account now ends that person's open sessions.

## Fixed

- **Deleting a user now signs them out immediately.** Until now the account
  disappeared from the Users page while the person's browser carried on working
  — with their old role, and their old access — until the session eventually
  timed out. For someone still using the app that could be the rest of the
  working day, because ordinary activity kept extending the session.

  Their very next action is now refused and they are signed out cleanly, the same
  way disabling an account already worked. The two look identical from outside,
  so nothing about a deleted account is disclosed.

- **That now covers the background keep-alive an open tab sends**, which had been
  quietly preventing a deleted account's session from ever expiring on its own.

- **The same gap after a full restore is closed.** A restore replaces every
  account, and any session open at the time previously kept working.

- **Deleting a user who has already been removed** now reports "User not found"
  rather than failing with a server error.

## Unchanged on purpose

- **Creating or restoring an account is unaffected.** A new user can sign in and
  start work straight away, and sessions already in progress are untouched.

- **A brief database outage does not sign anyone out.** The check deliberately
  errs towards keeping everyone working rather than locking out the whole system
  over a momentary hiccup — the same choice the existing account checks make.

## Also

- An internal build check was extended so that this class of gap fails the build
  instead of shipping quietly.

## Upgrading

No action needed.
